author: Bob Van Voris
description: Ousted Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro asked a federal judge to dismiss drug-trafficking charges against him, claiming the US government is blocking funds for his legal defense from the Venezuelan government.
title: Maduro Seeks to Toss US Charges Over Blocked Payments to Lawyer

description: Former US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton says she repeatedly told congressional investigators that she never met Jeffrey Epstein or had any connection with him. The former first lady was deposed behind closed doors. Clinton says she also touched on topics ranging from UFOs to the so-called PizzaGate conspiracy theory that took hold during the 2016 presidential campaign. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Hillary Clinton Says She Denied Ever Knowing Jeffrey Epstein

description: Anthropic said that new language proposed by the Pentagon as a compromise failed to satisfy the firm’s desire to preserve key safeguards that it has sought for any military use of its AI tools. Joe Mathieu reports on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Anthropic Rejects Pentagon's Latest Offer

author: Emily Mason, Katanga Johnson
description: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency proposed rules that would restrict companies from launching branded stablecoins through white-label platforms and offering rewards tied to them, the agency’s first major attempt to implement the federal cryptocurrency law signed by President Donald Trump in July.
title: Federal Bank Regulator Moves to Restrict US Stablecoin Rewards

description: House Democrats on Thursday demanded President Donald Trump follow the Clintons in testifying to congressional investigators on ties to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton began a closed-door deposition Thursday by a House panel investigating Epstein in Chappaqua in upstate New York, where she has a home with her husband, former President Bill Clinton, according to a person familiar with the proceedings. Bill Clinton is set to face questioning on Friday. Bloomberg News National Security Reporter Jamie Tarabay joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. She speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Democrats Demand Trump Follow Clintons on Epstein Testimony

author: David Gura, Rachael Lewis-Krisky
description: On today’s Big Take podcast: Trump said the US would “run” Venezuela after capturing Nicolás Maduro in January. What’s actually happened since?
title: What Trump’s Venezuela Plan Looks Like From Caracas

description: The Supreme Court’s decision blocking Donald Trump’s tariff strategy has thrown US trade policy into turmoil. As he scrambles for a new path, we look at what his trade war has accomplished. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: How Trump's Tariffs Got a Reality Check

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss Hillary Clinton’s Jeffrey Epstein testimony to congressional investigators with Bloomberg News National Security Reporter Jamie Tarabay. Then, Bloomberg's Kunjan Sobhani and Robert Schiffman from Bloomberg Intelligence join to discuss Nvidia's upbeat sales outlook still not seeming to deliver what Wall Street is looking for. Then, ‘Chip War’ Author Chris Miller on the global competition for AI dominance. Lastly, Dr. Joy Gelbman, Cardiologist at Weill Cornell Medicine, joins to discuss women's heart health and cardiovascular risks amid American Heart Month. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Nvidia Forecast Fails to Relieve Concerns | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 2/26/2026

author: Joe Sobczyk
description: The US is easing the way for American companies to sell fuel to private Cuban businesses.
title: Trump Looks to Leverage Cuba’s Energy Crisis to Gain Influence

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz discusses high-level talks between the US and Iran in Geneva. On today's show, Rapidan Energy Group Founder Bob McNally, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Former Special Assistant to President Joe Biden Meghan Hays and American Enterprise Institute Angela Stent. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Calls US Nuclear Talks Intense | Balance of Power: Early Edition 2/26/2026

author: Natalia Drozdiak, Ben Bartenstein, Kate Sullivan, Courtney McBride
description: President Donald Trump put his son-in-law Jared Kushner and longtime friend Steve Witkoff in charge of resolving the war in Ukraine and a standoff with Iran. On Thursday, they juggled those momentous issues within hours of each other.
title: Trump Puts Fate of World’s Top Conflicts in the Hands of Two Men

description: The number of US nationals applying for British citizenship hit an all-time high in the first year of President Donald Trump’s second term in the White House.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Applications For UK Citizenship Hit An All-Time High

author: Iain Marlow
description: The Pentagon escalated its ongoing dispute with Anthropic PBC on Thursday, making public a threat to effectively ban the artificial intelligence startup from the US military’s vast supply chain.
title: Pentagon Hardens Its Ultimatum to Anthropic in Feud Over AI Use

author: Patrick Sykes, Eltaf Najafizada
description: The US and Iran will continue nuclear talks next week after making “significant progress” in Switzerland, mediator Oman said, easing concerns about the potential for imminent military action by Washington.
title: US, Iran to Hold Talks Next Week After Progress in Geneva

author: Peter Chapman, Max Ramsay
description: The European Union’s anti-fraud office has been asked to “look into” the conduct of Peter Mandelson during his time as the bloc’s trade chief, after further details of the British politician’s links with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein came to light.
title: EU Commission Asks Anti-Fraud Watchdog to Probe Mandelson

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: The Pentagon’s first kamikaze drone unit is ready to participate if President Donald Trump decides to launch strikes on Iran, according to US officials and analysts.
title: First US Kamikaze Drone Unit Ready in Middle East

author: Eric Martin, Jim Wyss, Daniel Flatley
description: The Trump administration’s move to ease fuel shipments to Cuba’s nascent private sector is part of a plan to make the island more reliant on the US for supplies, increasing Washington’s leverage to bring about political and economic change, according to people familiar with the strategy.
title: Trump Aims to Steer Cuba Toward Greater Dependence on the US

author: Joe Mayes, Jess Shankleman
description: The UK Treasury is considering scrapping a windfall tax on North Sea oil and gas following persistent pushback from producers, according to a person familiar with the matter.
title: UK Holds Talks With Oil and Gas Producers on Ending Windfall Tax

author: Nojoud Al Mallees, Melissa Shin, Ari Altstedter
description: Canadian Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre says China cannot serve as a substitute for the US, rebuking Prime Minister Mark Carney’s recent outreach to the Asian superpower amid strained ties with the Trump administration.
title: China Cannot Replace US, Carney’s Conservative Rival Warns

author: Suzanne Monyak
description: President Donald Trump may continue constructing a 90,000-square-foot ballroom at the White House, a Washington federal judge held in a ruling that dealt an initial blow to historic preservationists who tried to halt the project.
title: Preservationists Lose Bid to Stop Trump White House Ballroom

author: Skylar Woodhouse, Myles Miller, Laura Nahmias
description: President Donald Trump plans to meet New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani Thursday at the White House, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Mamdani to Meet Trump at White House, Testing Budding Ties

author: Magdalena Del Valle
description: The Trump administration will pay more of the dues it owes to the United Nations as long as the world body keeps enacting reforms demanded by Washington, US Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz said.
title: Waltz Says UN Needs ‘Tough Love’ and Reforms to Get More US Cash

author: Daniel Carvalho, Martha Viotti Beck, Daniela Milanese, Andrew Rosati
description: Flavio Bolsonaro’s presidential candidacy is shifting into higher gear, surprising skeptics who initially didn’t believe his decision to run for Brazil’s top job was real.
title: Flavio Bolsonaro’s Rapid Rise in Brazil Presidential Polls Surprises Skeptics

description: Jonathan Tirone, Bloomberg News nuclear correspondent, breaks down the latest round of US-Iran nuclear talks. Iran says the meetings on Thursday progressed “very intensely and very seriously." Steve Witkoff is leading the talks for the US.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Says Nuclear Talks With US Were 'Very Intense and Serious'

author: Patrick Van Oosterom
description: Europe’s biggest port warned that it’s increasingly exposed to geopolitical risks related to trade with China.
title: EU’s Biggest Port Sees Geopolitical Risks Linked to China Trade

author: Jamie Tarabay
description: House Democrats on Thursday demanded President Donald Trump follow the Clintons in testifying to congressional investigators on ties to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.
title: Democrats Demand Trump Follow Clintons on Epstein Testimony

author: Leah Nylen, Jaewon Kang
description: Walmart Inc. agreed to pay $100 million Thursday to settle a lawsuit by the US Federal Trade Commission and a group of states alleging the company withheld tips and misrepresented wages to drivers who deliver orders as part of its Spark program.
title: Walmart to Pay $100 Million to Settle FTC Case on Driver Wages

author: Greg Stohr
description: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court for clearance to end legal protections that let almost 7,000 Syrians temporarily live and work in the US without risk of deportation.
title: Supreme Court Asked to Let US Lift Syrian Deportation Shield

description: Former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern is relocating to Australia, joining a wave of Kiwis moving across the Tasman. Rosalind Mathieson explains why the exodus is becoming a political issue. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: New Zealand Ex-PM Jacinda Ardern Joins Kiwi Exodus to Australia

author: Zoltan Simon
description: Hungary announced a police probe into the handling of toxic substances at Samsung SDI’s battery factory north of Budapest, after a contamination scandal engulfed Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s government weeks before closely fought elections.
title: Hungary Starts Battery Plant Probe as Scandal Hits Orban Rating

author: Madison Muller
description: US Food and Drug Administration Commissioner Marty Makary defended against accusations his top deputy is unfairly rejecting promising drugs, in a combative television interview with CNBC on Thursday that added to pressure the agency is facing over how it’s run.
title: FDA’s Makary Says Agency Is Facing a Media ‘Smear Campaign’

author: Foster Wong, Josh Xiao
description: China removed nine military lawmakers from its national parliament in the latest sign that President Xi Jinping’s purge of key defense establishment personnel continues to widen.
title: China Ousts Nine Military Lawmakers as Xi’s Defense Purge Widens

author: Lucy White
description: The number of US nationals applying for British citizenship hit an all-time high in the first year of President Donald Trump’s second term in the White House.
title: British Citizenship Applications by US Nationals Hit Record High

author: Ellen Milligan
description: The UK said it won’t implement a treaty handing the Chagos Islands to Mauritius without the support of the US, likely extending its delay due to Donald Trump’s new-found opposition to the deal.
title: UK Says It Won’t Proceed With Chagos Deal Without Trump Blessing

author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen
description: Israel and India will jointly produce weapons and intend to conclude a free trade agreement soon, a move that underscores deepening ties between the two countries.
title: India and Israel Boost Defense Ties, Finalize Trade Deal Soon

author: Stephan Kueffner
description: Ecuador announced plans to boost tariffs on imports from Colombia to 50% from 30% effective March 1, as part of an escalating dispute between the two Andean neighbors.
title: Ecuador Raises Punitive Tariffs on Colombian Imports to 50%

author: Piotr Skolimowski
description: Poland’s Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski signaled his country’s wide-eyed support for the US has reached its limits after President Donald Trump began redrawing the global order.
title: Poland Will Stay US Ally But Can’t Be a Sucker, Sikorski Says

author: Daniel Basteiro
description: The prime ministers of five European Union countries have called on the European Commission to act on a citizen-led initiative seeking funding to support access to abortion across the bloc.
title: Five EU Premiers Urge Commission to Fund Abortion Access

author: Todd Gillespie
description: US Senator Elizabeth Warren is stepping up pressure on regulators to investigate Wall Street executives who may have assisted convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
title: Goldman, JPMorgan Draw Elizabeth Warren’s Scrutiny Over Epstein

description: World Health Organization Chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus speaks to Bloomberg's Mishal Husain about the US stance on mRNA vaccine research funding. "I hope they will reconsider," he says on The Mishal Husain Show. He also talks about his relationship with US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., saying they "continue to speak to each other." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Is 'Wrong' to Defund mRNA Research, WHO Chief Says

author: Sanne Wass
description: Denmark’s Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen called an early election for March 24 after a standoff with Donald Trump over Greenland lifted her party’s standing in opinion polls.
title: Danish Leader Calls Snap Vote as Party Gains on Greenland Rift

author: Paul Vecchiatto
description: South Africa is preparing to deploy soldiers to help tackle gang violence and illegal mining, challenges the police have struggled to contain.
title: South Africa Readies Troops to Help Police Tackle Gang Violence

author: Anthony Halpin
description: US and Ukrainian officials meet in Geneva today to discuss a peace plan.
title: Putin Faces Stick-or-Twist Dilemma With Trump

author: Anna Edgerton, Michael Sasso, Christopher Cannon
description: Some Palmetto State Republicans are pushing for new Congressional maps to expand GOP dominance. Others fear unintended consequences.
title: South Carolina Redistricting Debate Shows Risks for Republicans

author: Michael Cohen
description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa’s plans to turn the country into a giant construction site are gathering pace, with the government ramping up spending on roads, power plants, dams and ports.
title: The Infrastructure Projects Transforming South African Landscape

author: Craig Stirling, Jana Randow, Mark Schroers
description: The European Central Bank will closely monitor for any signs that the adoption of artificial intelligence throughout the economy is sparking job losses, President Christine Lagarde said.
title: Lagarde Vows ‘Extremely Attentive’ ECB on AI-Driven Job Cuts

author: Patricia Laya
description: Most Venezuelans expect the economy and job market to improve within six months as the US eases sanctions and the government rolls out reforms to attract investment.
title: Venezuelans See Brighter Economic Outlook After US Intervention

author: Irina Anghel
description: The number of young Britons left out of work and education climbed closer to 1 million, as the Labour government’s policies attract criticism for stoking youth unemployment.
title: Nearly a Million Young Britons Are Not in Jobs or Education

author: Arne Delfs
description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he’ll push ahead with a new effort to strengthen Sino-German ties while highlighting the need to address “high capacities” in China that “far exceed market demand” and are problematic for Europe.
title: Merz Commits to Stronger China Ties on First Visit as Chancellor

author: Sakura Murakami
description: The US and Japan still need to do a lot of work to hammer the funding details for three projects announced as part of a US-Japan trade deal, according to the head of a Tokyo-backed bank involved in the negotiations.
title: US-Japan Investment Funding Still Needs Work, JBIC Chief Says

author: Philip Heijmans
description: Singapore’s total fertility rate fell to 0.87 in 2025, marking a record low that a top official warned could profoundly reshape the city-state’s society and economy.
title: Singapore’s Fertility Rate Falls to Fresh Low as Population Ages

author: Shruti Srivastava
description: US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick met his Indian counterpart in an unscheduled visit to New Delhi Thursday, days after the US Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump’s sweeping global tariffs.
title: Lutnick Makes Surprise Trip to India After US Tariff Setback

author: Donato Paolo Mancini
description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s coalition is closing in on an agreement to change Italy’s electoral system in a bid to improve her chances in the 2027 general election.
title: Meloni’s Coalition Nears Deal to Alter Italy’s Electoral Law

author: Olesia Safronova
description: Russia launched a massive drone and missile attack on Ukraine, hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and US counterpart Donald Trump discussed potential next steps in peace talks.
title: Russia Carries Out Massive Air Attack Ahead of Ukraine-US Talks

author: Erica Yokoyama
description: The Japanese government expects its interest payments on outstanding debt to roughly double over the next four years as the Bank of Japan’s gradual rate hikes push up borrowing costs.
title: Japan Sees Interest Payments Doubling by 2029 as BOJ Hikes Rate

author: Yusuke Maekawa, Tsuyoshi Inajima
description: Japan’s reliance on China for rare earths increased last month, despite a reduction in volumes purchased from the world’s dominant producer.
title: Japan Leans More on China for Rare Earths Despite Lower Imports

author: Antony Sguazzin
description: Ghana’s Foreign Minister Samuel Ablakwa said he visited Kyiv and held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy seeking the release of citizens of the African country who are being held as prisoners of war.
title: Ghana Minister Asks Zelenskiy to Release Captured Citizens

description:
On today's show, Nvidia has failed to impress investors with its latest sales forecast. The chipmaker delivered a first-quarter outlook that easily beat average estimates, but there was little change in the shares, over concerns about an overheated AI economy.

Cuban forces killed four people on a speedboat with Florida tags, an incident the US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said was being investigated and risks escalating tensions with the United States. Havana said the 10 people on board were carrying weapons and planned an uprising.

The US imposed sanctions on more than 30 entities that support Iranian oil and weapons sales ahead of nuclear talks today in Geneva.

Today's guests: Axa CEO Thomas Buberl & Chris Beauchamp, Chief Market Analyst at IG Group. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Nvidia Fails to Wow & Cuba Shootout With US Boat | Daybreak Europe 02/26/2026

author: Vlad Savov
description: OpenAI said its ChatGPT AI service refused to assist an individual associated with Chinese law enforcement in planning an online campaign to discredit the Japanese prime minister.
title: OpenAI Says ChatGPT Refused to Help Chinese Influence Operations

description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz met Chinese President Xi Jinping for the first time Wednesday, expressing optimism that the two countries can overcome disagreements on trade and geopolitics to forge a strategic partnership. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Merz, Xi Meeting: What's Next for Germany-China Ties?

author: Patrick Sykes
description: The US and Iran are set to hold a third round of nuclear talks on Thursday with days to go until President Donald Trump’s deadline for a deal.
title: US, Iran to Hold Nuclear Talks as Trump’s Deal Deadline Looms

description: US and Iranian diplomats are in Geneva in an effort to avert renewed hostilities. If negotiations collapse, US President Donald Trump has signaled he’s prepared to escalate, backed by a large military buildup in the region. Meanwhile, satellite images taken this month show Iranian engineers clearing debris at nuclear facilities damaged during last June’s 12-day conflict with the US and Israel, while reinforcing key sites against future attacks. Bloomberg's Patrick Sykes reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran-US Talks to Resume in Geneva

author: Simona Weinglass
description: Authorities say a citizen spent almost a million dollars promoting a pro-Russia candidate by giving in-app gifts.
title: Did Romania’s ‘King of TikTok’ Really Sway a Presidential Election?

description: Addressing one of his biggest audiences at perhaps the lowest moment of his second term, President Donald Trump returned again and again in his State of the Union speech to the same message on the economy: Everything is going great.  A resolute Trump was determined to will Americans into a better economic mood, seeking to paint over the affordability concerns at the center of upcoming midterm elections with statistics and self-congratulation. "Inflation is plummeting. Incomes are rising fast. The roaring economy is roaring like never before," Trump boasted early in the nearly two-hour speech. Bloomberg Opinion Senior Executive Editor Tim O'Brien joins Stephen Carroll and Lizzy Burden on Daybreak Europe Radio with his thoughts. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump's State Of The Union 'Avoided Issues' Says Tim O'Brien

description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a strengthening of defense, trade and counter-terrorism ties with Israel during a rare visit — his first in nine years. Defense relations between the nations are an “important pillar” of the partnership, Modi said in an address to the Knesset, Israel’s parliament, after arriving in Tel Aviv where he was met by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Bloomberg's Dan Williams reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Modi Meets Netanyahu to Strengthen Defense, Trade Ties

author: Katarina Hoije
description: The tri-border region of Nigeria, Benin and Niger is becoming a new stronghold for jihadists, as militants turn forests and pastoral networks in West Africa into bases for recruitment and international attacks.
title: Jihadists Turn Coastal West Africa Borderlands Into Strongholds

author: Erica Yokoyama
description: Births in Japan fell for a 10th straight year in 2025 underscoring the demographic strain Japan faces as Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi pursues new measures to counter the decline.
title: Japan’s Births Fall for 10th Year Adding to Demographic Strain

author: Jonathan Tirone, Raeedah Wahid, Hayley Warren, Rachel Lavin
description: If it decides to attack, the US would face a complicated set of targets because of Iran’s rugged geography and its efforts to protect military assets.
title: Satellite Images Expose Trump’s Claim of ‘Easy’ Victory in Iran

author: Nectar Gan
description: A Hong Kong court has overturned former media mogul Jimmy Lai’s conviction in a fraud case, in a rare win for the pro-democracy advocate serving a 20-year sentence for national security charges.
title: Hong Kong’s Jimmy Lai Wins Rare Appeal Over Fraud Conviction

author: Mirette Magdy
description: Egypt unlocked about $2.3 billion in loans after clearing reviews of an International Monetary Fund program that was expanded in 2024, a boost for a country whose currency and bonds have felt jitters over the prospect of a US-Iran war.
title: Egypt Unlocks Around $2.3 Billion in IMF Funding After Reviews

author: Jimmy Jenkins, Chris Strohm
description: Two Democratic secretaries of state said they were told the Trump administration isn’t planning to send federal immigration enforcement agents to polling locations during November’s congressional elections.
title: States Are Told ICE Won’t Target Polling Stations in November

author: Ainsley Thomson
description: Former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern and her family are relocating to Australia, becoming the most high-profile addition to a growing wave of Kiwis moving across the Tasman.
title: New Zealand Ex-PM Jacinda Ardern Joins Kiwi Exodus to Australia

author: Brian Platt, Laura Dhillon Kane
description: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s visit to India this week will cement a diplomatic reset and unlock a wave of new trade opportunities, including in nuclear power, oil and critical minerals, India’s top diplomat to Canada said.
title: India, Canada to Sign ‘Immense’ Range of Deals During Carney Visit

author: Daniel Cancel
description: Cuba says a boat with 10 people near its coast early Wednesday was carrying weapons, and its occupants — Cubans living in the US — were intent on entering the country to fight against the government.
title: Cuba Says Those Killed in US Boat Encounter Planned Uprising

author: Katrina Manson, Maggie Eastland, Kendall Taggart
description: The high-stakes conflict between the Defense Department and a $380 billion tech powerhouse goes to the heart of just how far AI can go in warfare.
title: Anthropic’s Pentagon Showdown Is About More Than AI Guardrails

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Patrick McHenry, former US Representative (R-NC) shares his reaction to President Trump's State of the Union address. Senator Roger Marshall (R-KS) states President Trump’s speech gave a feeling of empathy and hope. Rep. Joe Morelle (D-NY) talks about the latest on DHS funding and the partial government shutdown. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Defends His Policies in State of the Union | Balance of Show: Late Edition 02/25/2026

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: Kim Jong Un pledged to build more nuclear weapons and upgrade his missile programs but said it could also be possible to improve relations with the US if Washington recognizes North Korea as a nuclear power.
title: North Korea’s Kim Vows to Build More Nukes, But Opens Door to US

author: Laura Avetisyan, Alex Morales
description: Residents of suburban Manchester head to the polling booths on Thursday to vote in a parliamentary election that threatens to lay bare the danger posed to UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s Labour Party from both the political right and left.
title: Three-Way Manchester Contest Highlights Peril for Starmer in UK
